title: observability: exporter rotation, remote_write sharding, and alert autoscale for private installs
author: Jordan Patel
description: Motivation: Private installs running high-cardinality workloads (customer embeddings, per-tenant metrics) hit Prometheus remote_write/ingestion bottlenecks and cause alert storms during upgrades. This PR implements three operational features to make observability upgrades and high-throughput installs safer: 1) exporter rotation orchestration that drains and replaces metrics exporters (node-exporter/prometheus-exporter sidecars) during upgrades to avoid double-scrape spikes and gaps; 2) remote_write sharding support in the Terraform module + Prometheus Helm values so high-cardinality telemetry can be sharded across multiple remote_write receivers/backends; 3) alert autoscale policy and Alertmanager replica rotation to prevent alert floods from bringing down control plane components. Summary of changes and approach: - Helm: add values.exporterRotation.{enabled,drainTimeout,preStopHookScript} controlling a preStop lifecycle script that signals exporter sidecars to stop emitting for a short window and waits for Prometheus to complete pending scrapes. Also add prometheus.remoteWrite.shards and prometheus.remoteWrite.shardKey settings and templates to render multiple remote_write targets. - Terraform: extend modules/observability with variable remote_write_shards (default 1), remote_write_targets (list of endpoints) and create a lightweight sharding plan that generates k8s Secret + Service resources for each shard when shards>1. Also add upgrade-safe lifecycle for Grafana deployments to rotate pods with a configurable maxUnavailable and annotation-based rotation marker. - Installer orchestration: add a new hook (scripts/rotate_exporters.sh) used by Helm hooks and by the installer upgrade pipeline to perform a coordinated rotation: mark exporters read-only, wait for KV cache flushes and Prometheus scrape windows, then scale down old exporters and scale up new ones. Hook is idempotent and logs to /var/log/redwood-observability-rotate.log. - Alerting: add a horizontal-pod-autoscaler template for Alertmanager that uses a custom metric (alerts_per_min) collected by a tiny exporter; include default thresholds and a fallback to fixed replicas when metrics are absent. Also include a rate-limiting rule and default grouping/routing templates to cut alert storms during rollout windows. Backwards compatibility and upgrade notes: the changes are opt-in via new installer flags (observability.exporterRotation.enabled and observability.remoteWrite.shards) so existing customers won't see behavior changes unless they enable them. The Terraform module supports a migration path: with remote_write_shards set to >1 the installer will create additional k8s Services and Secrets; a one-time run of 'terraform apply' will materialize shards. Rollback plan: helm rollback will disable rotation hooks via a release annotation the hook checks; Terraform changes are additive (create-only) and removed on shard count=1. Tests and validation: - Unit tests for terraform templates and helm templating added. - Integration e2e run in the private-installer CI staging cluster validated exporter rotation with a synthetic 50k series workload and confirmed no more than 2% scrape loss during rotation. - Manual runbook added to docs/upgrade-observability-rotation.md. Monitoring and observability: added metrics for rotation progress (rotation_in_progress, exporters_drained_count), Prometheus recording rules for alert autoscale triggers, and Grafana dashboard panels to visualize shard distribution and rotation state. Why this is different from previous provisioning work: earlier PRs focused on bootstrapping stacks and provisioning dashboards; this PR focuses on operational safety and runtime scaling for high-cardinality customers and upgrade windows, providing automated, reversible operations for on-prem and VPC private installs.

release_notes: Added exporter rotation orchestration for safe upgrades, support for sharded Prometheus remote_write via Terraform and Helm, Alertmanager autoscaling with alert-throttling templates, and runbook for enabling these features in private installs.
notes_for_ops: Operators enabling sharding must provide remote_write endpoints in installer config and ensure downstream storage can accept shard-specific keys. For upgrades, run the rotation in a maintenance window and monitor rotation_in_progress metric. The rotation script writes detailed logs to /var/log/redwood-observability-rotate.log.
